title: Rust: Stack (LIFO)
description: Implement a stack data structure using Vec and the LIFO principle.

steps.title: Stack Using Vec
steps.description: Create a `Vec<i32>` and use `.push()` to add 10, 20, 30. Print the Vec.

steps.title: Pop from Stack
steps.description: Pop elements from the stack using `.pop()` until it's empty. Print each popped value.
hints: Use `while let Some(value) = stack.pop() { println!("{}", value); }`

verification.failureMessage: Pop and print all elements (should be 30, 20, 10).

steps.title: Peek at Top
steps.description: Show the top of the stack without removing it using `.last()` or `.peek()`. Push 1, 2, 3 and peek after each push.
hints: `.last()` peeks at the last element without removing.
After pushing 1: top=1, after pushing 2: top=2, etc.

verification.failureMessage: Print the top of the stack after each push.

steps.title: Check Balanced Parentheses
steps.description: Write a function `is_balanced(s: &str) -> bool` that checks if parentheses are balanced using a stack. Test with `"()()"`, `"(()"`, `")("`.
hints: For '(' push, for ')' pop. If pop returns None, it's unbalanced.
At the end, the stack should be empty.
Use a Vec<char> as the stack.

steps.title: Custom Stack Struct
steps.description: Define a generic `Stack<T>` struct wrapping Vec<T> with methods `push`, `pop`, `peek`, `is_empty`, and `len`. Test by reversing a string using the stack.
hints: Reverse string: push all chars, then pop all chars.

verification.successMessage: Custom Stack struct and string reversal work!
verification.failureMessage: Use your Stack to reverse 'hello' and print 'olleh'.
